name: Citizenship by Descent or Birth in Territory

requirements.blocker_text: Law No. 24 of 2010, Article 3(a): any person born in Libya to a Libyan father is Libyan. Article 3(b) extends this to a person born OUTSIDE Libya to a Libyan father, provided the birth is registered within one year. This transmission is automatic and unconditional.
requirements.fix_path: Establish paternal filiation to a Libyan father via a birth certificate (registered within 1 year of birth if born abroad).

requirement_groups.name: Child of a Libyan mother, father unknown or stateless

requirements.blocker_text: Article 3(c): nationality passes through a Libyan mother only in limited circumstances -- where the father's nationality is unknown, the father was without a nationality, or both parents are unknown (a foundling-type case). This is NOT a general mother-to-child transmission right equivalent to Article 3(a)'s father-based rule -- a materially starker gender asymmetry than the marriage-based asymmetries found in other countries this dataset (e.g. Cameroon, Congo-Brazzaville, Iraq), because here the asymmetry sits in the DESCENT rule itself, not only in a marriage-based acquisition track.
requirements.fix_path: Establish maternal filiation to a Libyan mother where the father's nationality is unknown, the father is stateless, or both parents are unknown.

requirement_groups.name: Child of a Libyan mother married to a non-Libyan father (discretionary)

requirements.blocker_text: Article 11: a child of a Libyan mother married to a non-Libyan father 'may be granted' Libyan nationality through a regulatory procedure -- this is explicitly discretionary, not an automatic entitlement, and this dataset could not locate the implementing regulation describing the actual criteria or approval rate.
requirements.fix_path: Apply through the regulatory procedure referenced in Article 11; the specific implementing criteria could not be confirmed in this build.

evidence_required.document: Birth certificate showing paternal or (exceptional) maternal filiation
Proof of father's unknown nationality or statelessness (exceptional maternal route only)

sources.title: Global Citizenship Observatory (GLOBALCIT, an EU-affiliated academic research consortium) -- English translation of Libya's Law No. 24 of 2010 on Libyan Nationality: descent (Art. 3), discretionary maternal transmission (Art. 11), naturalization (Art. 9/10), dual nationality restrictions (Art. 5)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Libya). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier 2 (an academic/research-consortium host of an unofficial English translation, not a .gov.ly domain); the validator requires tier-1 sourcing for a hard requirement before publishing, so this is correctly modeled as draft from the outset. GENUINE, SEVERE GENDER ASYMMETRY -- the starkest found in this dataset to date: unlike every other country built this session (where descent itself is gender-neutral and only marriage-based citizenship acquisition is asymmetric), Libya's DESCENT rule itself favors the father -- a Libyan father transmits nationality automatically and unconditionally, while a Libyan mother only transmits it in narrow exceptional circumstances (father unknown/stateless, or both parents unknown), with the broader case of a Libyan mother married to a known foreign father left to full government discretion (Article 11) rather than any entitlement. dual_citizenship_allowed set to false per Article 5 (voluntary acquisition of a foreign nationality without prior government approval triggers deprivation of Libyan nationality) -- though Article 3(b) creates a narrow, disclosed exception for a minor child born abroad to a Libyan father, who is not automatically deprived and may choose the foreign nationality only upon reaching adulthood.
